Hi Samir / Alicia — great to meet you both yesterday. Thanks for the thoughtful questions; answers below and next steps at the bottom.

1) PO vs card/invoice
- For hosted API (our hosted Redwood API) we support both card and invoiced billing / PO for customers on an approved credit / enterprise arrangement. Typical payment term is net-30 for invoice/PO flows.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments we require an enterprise contract (MSA + SOW) and billing is usually handled via PO/invoice.

2) Marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure)
- AWS Marketplace: yes — Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace for our hosted offering. Purchasing via AWS Marketplace (Private Offers or SaaS contracts) is a common path for faster procurement and consolidated billing. I'll confirm the exact listing ID with our ops team (cc'd: Dev).
- GCP Marketplace: we have a published offering in pilot for the US region; adoption is growing but some enterprise features (dedicated capacity) still route direct.
- Azure Marketplace: work in progress with a partner reseller; plausible but not the fastest path today.

3) Dedicated/Private path
- Dedicated/Private typically needs an MSA and SOW. We can offer a standard MSA + a template SOW; turnaround is usually 2–3 weeks for procurement/legal review at companies of your size, sometimes faster with an existing PO process.

Attachments: RWI-pricing-2026-03.pdf (pricing + seat/bandwidth tiers), SOC2-TypeII-Report-Redwood.pdf (audit report).

Suggested next steps:
- Dev to confirm AWS Marketplace listing ID and whether a Private Offer is required to get consolidated billing.
- If you prefer the fastest path, start with an AWS Marketplace purchase for the hosted API pilot (no MSA required for small pilots).
- If you prefer Dedicated/Private for data isolation, we can spin up an MSA + SOW and provide a draft in 48hrs.

Dev — can you confirm the AWS listing ID and whether we support Private Offer creation for Acme?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Commercial paths (summary):
1) AWS Marketplace (fastest for pilots)
   - Pros: fastest procurement, consolidated billing via AWS, can use Private Offer for negotiated pricing, minimal contract friction for small pilots.
   - Cons: some enterprise features (Dedicated/Private) may still require a direct SOW/MSA if you need isolated capacity.

2) Direct PO + MSA (recommended for Dedicated/Private)
   - Pros: supports Dedicated/Private deployments, flexibility on SOW terms, invoiced billing with net-30, Redwood signs MSA.
   - Cons: longer legal procurement cycle (typical 2–3 weeks).
